units.section: INTRO
units.spoken: Soft Actor-Critic (SAC)

units.section: INTRO
units.spoken: A network that sets a robot's turning forces keeps a range of choices and earns a reward for staying undecided.

sections.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: Section one, Why commit to one set of forces

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: Staying undecided instead of adding noise

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: Picture a robot arm that must try new torques, but every wild swing costs time and can damage it. Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) commits to one set of turning forces, so it needs noise added from outside to try new ones.

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: Soft Actor-Critic (SAC) lets the network that picks the forces keep a range instead, so it explores by drawing from that range. Soft means staying undecided earns a bonus on top of the reward.

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: When it works, the arm tries nearby torques on its own, without a random kick from outside.

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: 1.1 Fixed noise is one more setting to tune

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: Picture the Reacher arm trying a move: the agent, the learner picking the moves, reads the state, the arm's angles and speeds right now, picks a move, one choice it can make in that state, and the world hands back a reward, a number saying how good the move was, and the arm learns from the return.

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: The running example is the Reacher task: a robot arm with two joints whose actions are four torques. A torque is a turning force a motor applies at a joint. On the Reacher each torque is a number from -1 to 1. Each joint can turn about two axes, so each joint gets two torques. Every step the arm senses its state, numbers describing the position, rotation and speed of its parts, and earns a small reward whenever its hand is inside a moving goal.

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: Let's take a look at figure 1. The Reacher arm has a shoulder joint and an elbow joint, and each joint turns about two axes, so the arm picks four torques in all. The hand has to sit inside a moving goal to earn its small reward. So the arm senses its state, picks four torques from -1 to 1, and earns a small reward whenever its hand sits inside the moving goal.

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: The arm senses its state, picks four torques from -1 to 1, and earns a small reward whenever its hand sits inside the moving goal. With the goal up and to the right, the shoulder turns the upper arm toward it and the elbow bends the forearm until the hand lands inside the goal circle.

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: The return is all the reward still to come, with later rewards counted a little less. A move's value Q of s and a, also called its score, is the return the agent expects if it makes move a in state s and plays on from there. So the hand must follow the goal as it moves, not just reach it once.

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: DDPG and TD3 learn two kinds of network. The deterministic actor mu sub thay-ta is a network with weights thay-ta that outputs one action every time, with no random draw. The critic Q sub fee is a network with weights fee that scores a state and an action together; its score stands for the return the agent expects. Both networks learn from the steps the arm has already taken.

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: DDPG and TD3 explore by adding noise to that one set of torques. Exploration noise is a small random nudge added to the actor's actions while it learns, so the agent tries moves it is not sure about. On a real robot every one of those random tries costs time and wear.

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: 1.2 Every step costs on a real robot

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: The Minitaur is a small four-legged robot with eight motors, two per leg. Its actions are each leg's swing angle and extension, which a low-level controller turns into motor positions. Each fall costs time and can damage it, so the learner must reuse old steps and explore without wild moves.

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: Let's take a look at figure 2. The Minitaur is a small four-legged robot with eight motors, two per leg. It is shown on four surfaces: flat ground, a slope, wooden blocks and stairs. So the same gait, a way of walking, must keep working on all four surfaces, and on stairs a wild swing can topple the robot.

units.section: 1 Why commit to one set of forces
units.spoken: Figure 2 shows the Minitaur on flat ground, a slope, wooden blocks and stairs, four surfaces where the same gait, a way of walking, must keep working. On stairs a wild swing can topple the robot.

sections.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: Section two, A range of torques instead of one torque

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: The Gaussian actor

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: Picture the Reacher arm's four torques as a bell: most draws land near the middle, a few land further out.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: A Gaussian actor outputs one centre and one width per torque and draws each torque from that bell, so the width is learned, not a noise size set by hand.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: When it works, the bell starts wide while the arm is unsure and narrows as the reach improves.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: 2.1 The actor draws each torque from a bell

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: Let's take a look at figure 3. The bell of torques has a centre and a width. Most draws land near the centre, and a few land further out. So the actor draws each torque from the bell, and the width is learned, not a noise size set by hand.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: We write SAC's actor as pee sub thay-ta, with weights thay-ta, because it draws its torques by chance; mu sub thay-ta is the actor that outputs one action every time.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: The tanh function squashes any number into -1 to 1, the torque range. Each draw is then squashed, so every torque stays in range.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: 2.2 Staying undecided earns a bonus

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: Entropy and the entropy bonus

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: Picture the bell wide and the arm still unsure which torque is best. A policy is the agent's rule for choosing a move in each state. Entropy H is how undecided the policy is; for a bell of torques, it is how wide the bell is.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: The entropy bonus is a small extra term that rewards staying undecided, which SAC adds to each step's reward, so a wider bell earns more of it.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: When it works, several good ways of moving stay alive instead of one fragile gait locking in too early.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: 2.3 The temperature weighs staying undecided against reward

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: The temperature

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: Picture the arm weighing two things: the reward for reaching the goal, and the bonus for staying undecided. The temperature alpha sets how much staying undecided is worth against reward.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: A higher temperature makes the bonus count for more, so the bell stays wider; a lower temperature makes reward count for more, so the bell narrows.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: When it works, the bell stays as wide as the task needs: wide enough to keep trying, narrow enough to commit.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: 2.4 The critic's target

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: The critic learns by being pulled toward a target, the step's reward plus its own score for what comes next, counted a little less. SAC also keeps the two critics of Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3), but not its other two changes. Delayed policy updates move the actor and the slow copies, copies of the networks updated only a little at a time, only once every few critic updates. Target policy smoothing adds a small random nudge to the next torques inside the target, clipped, meaning cut off at a fixed limit so the nudge stays small.

units.section: 2 A range of torques instead of one torque
units.spoken: Each change fixes one way the critic's errors leak into the actor. Delayed updates let the critic settle before the actor moves, so the actor never chases a critic that is still wrong. Smoothing makes the target average over nearby torques, so the actor cannot exploit one sharp peak in the critic's score. SAC needs neither: its actor already draws from a bell, so the target averages over a range of next torques, and the entropy bonus keeps the bell open.

sections.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Section three, How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: 3.1 Reward plus how undecided the policy is

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The objective: reward plus staying undecided

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Picture one run of the arm, step after step, each step earning a reward and a bonus for staying undecided. SAC scores each draw's surprise as its bonus, so the whole run is judged by reward plus bonus.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The score adds the reward plus the temperature times the average surprise over every draw the bell might make, over every step of the run.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: When it works, a bell that keeps trying different torques scores higher than one that repeats a single miss.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Replay, also called the replay buffer, keeps a memory of past steps, and training draws random batches from it. The sign tilde means drawn at random from. log pee sub thay-ta of a given s is the log of how likely the actor was to draw this action from its bell, the height of the bell at that action; very negative means an unlikely draw, which happens more often when the bell is wide.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Equation 1. The objective. The arm is learning to reach for its target, and this equation is what counts whether one way of reaching beats another.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Take a look at this equation. The arm is learning to reach for its target, and this equation is what counts whether one way of reaching beats another.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The first line. J is the score the actor climbs. Pee sub thay-ta is the policy that picks the torques. Thay-ta is the set of weights that defines the policy. So the objective is the score to raise, and it is named J.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Intuition. The actor needs one number that says how good a whole way of reaching is, counting both the reward and the bonus for staying undecided.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The mathematics. J of pee sub thay-ta is the score the actor is trained to raise, for the policy pee sub thay-ta , the actor's bell of torques with weights thay-ta . The equals sign points to the next line, which says how that score is counted. So this line says: the score to raise is J .

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Example. Before the hand finds the goal the reward is small, but the bonus still counts at every step, so a bell that keeps trying different torques scores higher than one that repeats a single miss.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The second line. Sum over t adds over every step of the run. E is the average over what the actor might do. r sub t plus 1 is the reward after step t. H sub t is the surprise at step t. Alpha is the temperature that weighs surprise against reward. s sub t is the state at step t. So the score adds the reward and the temperature times the surprise, step by step.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Intuition. The score adds up over every step of a run, so staying undecided the whole time earns the bonus again and again.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The mathematics. The sum over t adds over every step t of an episode, one run from start to end. The E is the average over what the actor might do: each state and each torque it might draw there, weighted by its chance, and the sum over t adds those step averages. r sub t plus 1 is the reward that follows the step- t action, the small reward for keeping the hand on the goal. H sub t is the entropy in state s sub t , how undecided the policy is there. alpha is the temperature, how much staying undecided is worth against reward. With alpha at zero this is the sum of rewards. So this line says: add reward plus the temperature times surprise over every step.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Example. Take one step where the hand sits on the goal: the bonus is big when the bell is wide, so that step's average beats a narrow bell's.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The third line. h is the surprise of one draw. Pee sub thay-ta is the policy that picks the torques. a is the torque drawn. s sub t is the state at step t. So the surprise is minus the log of how likely the draw was.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Intuition. One draw can be scored for how surprising it was: a draw the bell was almost sure to make scores low, a rare draw scores high.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The mathematics. h is the surprise of one draw. pee sub thay-ta of a given s sub t is how likely the actor was to draw the torques a in the state s sub t , the height of its bell at that draw. The log of a likely draw is near zero, so h is small; the log of an unlikely draw is very negative, so minus the log makes h big. That is why h measures how unlikely one draw was. So this line says: minus the log of the draw's chance is its surprise.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Example. A draw near the centre of a wide bell is likely, so its surprise is small; a draw out at the edge is unlikely, so its surprise is big.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The fourth line. H sub t is the average surprise at step t. E is the average over the torques the bell might draw. a is the torque drawn. Pee sub thay-ta is the policy that picks the torques. h is each draw's surprise. So the surprise at each step is the average surprise over the torques the policy draws.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Intuition. The bonus for one draw is not enough: the score needs the average surprise over every draw the bell might make.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The mathematics. H sub t is the average surprise at step t . The E is the average over the torques the bell might draw, weighted by their chance. The average runs over the torques a from the actor's own bell pee sub thay-ta ; the tilde means drawn at random from, and h is each draw's surprise, which is minus the log of the draw's chance. A wide bell draws unlikely torques often, so its average is big; a narrow bell draws likely ones, so its average is small. So the whole equation says this: the score is reward plus the temperature times the average surprise, added over the run.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Example. At the start of training the bell is wide and the average surprise is big; as the reach improves the bell narrows and the average surprise falls, so the bonus fades as the arm commits.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: So the score to raise is the reward plus the temperature times the average surprise, added over every step of the run.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Take the arm reaching with its hand short of the goal. A policy that always pulls the same way earns the reward whenever the hand stays on the goal, but its surprise is small, so it adds almost no bonus. A policy that keeps its torques varied earns the same reward and a bigger bonus, because its draws are unlikely ones. The score in this equation prefers the second policy while the hand is learning its way to the goal.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: 3.2 A target that rewards staying undecided

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Slow copies and the soft update

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Picture the critic learning from a target that moves whenever the critic moves: it chases its own changes. A slow copy of a network is a copy updated only a little at a time, so its target holds almost still.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The soft update blends a small share tau of the live weights, the weights of the networks being trained, into each slow copy after each update, instead of overwriting it.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: When it works, the critic's scores settle toward a target that barely moves, instead of chasing their own changes.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The target

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Picture one stored step, the arm's hand near the goal. The critic learns by being pulled toward a target, the step's reward plus its own score for what comes next, counted a little less.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: SAC's target draws fresh next torques, keeps the lower of the two slow critics' scores for them, adds the temperature times the fresh draw's surprise, and discounts that future value onto the stored reward.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: When it works, a wide bell earns the bigger bonus on average, so the target rewards staying undecided.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: In DDPG both the actor and the critic have a slow copy, marked by a prime on the weights; SAC keeps only the slow critics, because its next torques come from a fresh draw.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Soft in Soft Actor-Critic means a move's value counts the entropy bonus; it is unrelated to the soft update that blends slow copies.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Equation 2. The target. The critics learn by being pulled toward a target, so each critic update needs a number to aim at. For the arm reaching for its target, each stored step needs that number before the critics can learn from it.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Take a look at this equation. The critics learn by being pulled toward a target, so each critic update needs a number to aim at. For the arm reaching for its target, each stored step needs that number before the critics can learn from it.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The first line. a prime is the fresh torque drawn for the next state. Pee sub thay-ta is the policy that picks the torques. s prime is the next state. So the target starts by drawing a fresh torque for the next state.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Intuition. The target needs next torques, but there is no slow actor to give them, so the live actor draws fresh ones for the next state.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The mathematics. a prime is the next torques, drawn at random, the tilde meaning drawn from, from the live actor's bell pee sub thay-ta in the next state s prime . The dot means over every possible torque: pee sub thay-ta of dot given s prime is the whole bell in state s prime , not one named torque. So this line says: draw the next torques from the live actor's bell in the next state.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Example. One next state gives its bell, and the draw lands somewhere inside it, not at its centre and not at a torque the arm cannot give.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The second line. q prime is the lower slow score. Min over i equals 1, 2 takes the lower of the two scores. Q sub fee prime sub i is the slow critic number i. s prime is the next state. a prime is the fresh torque drawn for the next state. So the slow score is the lower of the two slow critics on the next state and the fresh torque.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Intuition. One critic on its own can lift the target with an optimistic guess, so the target keeps the lower of the two slow scores.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The mathematics. q prime is the lower of the two slow scores. Min over i equals 1, 2 takes the lower of the two scores, with i running over critics 1 and 2. Q sub fee prime sub i are the two slow critics, the prime marking a slow copy, each scoring the next state s prime with the drawn torques a prime . Taking the lower guards the target, as in TD3, so one critic's optimistic guess cannot lift the target on its own. So this line says: keep the lower slow score.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Example. One slow critic scores the drawn torques high and the other scores them low; the lower score goes into the target and the high guess is ignored.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The third line. h prime is the surprise of the fresh draw. Pee sub thay-ta is the policy that picks the torques. a prime is the fresh torque drawn for the next state. s prime is the next state. So the surprise is minus the log of how likely the fresh draw was.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Intuition. The target's bonus needs one draw's surprise, measured on the same fresh draw the slow critics just scored.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The mathematics. h prime is the surprise of the fresh draw. pee sub thay-ta of a prime given s prime is how likely the live actor was to draw the torques a prime in the next state s prime . A likely draw makes h prime small and an unlikely draw makes it big, so h prime is one sample of the surprise h , which is minus the log of the draw's chance. So this line says: minus the log of the fresh draw's chance is its surprise.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Example. A fresh draw far from the bell's centre is unlikely, so its surprise is big and the target earns a bigger bonus for it.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The fourth line. y is the target the critic moves toward. r is the stored reward. q prime is the lower slow score. Alpha is the temperature that weighs surprise against reward. h prime is the surprise of the fresh draw. Gamma is the discount on the future. So the target is the stored reward plus the discounted lower slow score and the surprise bonus.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Intuition. Each stored step needs one number to aim at, built from its reward and what the next state promises.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The mathematics. y is the target for one stored step. r is this step's stored reward. Inside the bracket, q prime is the lower slow score, the lower of the two slow critics' scores, and alpha h prime is the bonus, the temperature times the surprise. gamma is the discount, how much a reward one step later still counts, so the future value counts a little less. The bonus measures how undecided the live actor is, so the next torques come from its own bell. This is the objective written one step at a time. So the whole equation says this: draw fresh next torques, keep the lower slow score, add the surprise bonus, and discount it onto the stored reward.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Example. One stored step brings its small reward, and the bracket adds the discounted lower score plus the bonus for the fresh draw, so the target is ready before the critics move.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: So the target for one stored step is the stored reward plus the discounted lower slow score and the surprise bonus.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Take a stored step where the arm's hand was near the goal and the next state leaves it still short. The target draws fresh torques for that next state, keeps the lower of the two slow scores, and adds a bonus that is big when the draw was an unlikely one.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Both live critics then move toward y by shrinking the squared gap between their score and y.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: 3.3 The actor's draw

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The reparameterized draw

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Picture a torque picked by chance: it has no smooth rule linking it to the actor's weights. The critic's slope, the direction its score rises as the torques change, cannot pass back through it.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The reparameterization trick writes a random draw as the centre plus the width times a fixed random number, so the critic's slope can flow back into the actor.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: When it works, each fresh draw lands near the centre but never the same twice, and the squashed torques stay inside what the joints can give.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Equation 3. The actor's draw. The draw must stay a smooth function of the actor's weights, so the critic's slope can flow back through it.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Take a look at this equation. The draw must stay a smooth function of the actor's weights, so the critic's slope can flow back through it.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The first line. u is the unsquashed draw. m sub thay-ta is the centre of the bell. Sigma sub thay-ta is the width of the bell. Thay-ta is the set of weights that defines the policy. s is the state. xi is a fresh random number. So the unsquashed draw is the centre plus the width times a fresh random number.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Intuition. A random draw has no smooth link to the actor's weights, so the draw is rebuilt as the centre plus the width times a fixed random number.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The mathematics. u is the unsquashed draw. m sub thay-ta of s is the centre, one per torque, and sigma sub thay-ta of s is the width, one per torque, both from the actor network with weights thay-ta for the state s . xi is a fresh random number drawn from a standard normal bell, one per torque, drawn independently; standard means the bell is centred at zero and its width is set to one. The width scales the draw and the centre shifts it. Moving the randomness into the fixed input xi makes the torques a smooth function of the actor's weights, so the critic's slope can flow back into them. So this line says: the centre plus the width times a fresh random number is the unsquashed draw.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Example. One state gives its centre and width, and a fresh random number picks a point inside the bell, so each draw is near the centre but never the same twice.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The second line. a is the torque drawn. Tanh squashes any number into -1 to 1. u is the unsquashed draw. So the squash keeps each torque inside what the arm can give.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Intuition. The unsquashed draw can grow past what the joints can give, so it is squashed into the torque range before the arm plays it.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The mathematics. a is the squashed draw. Tanh squashes any number into -1 to 1. The unsquashed draw u is the centre plus the width times a fresh random number, so however big it grows, the torques a stay inside what the arm can give. Slopes pass through the unsquashed draw and the squashing into the actor, so the actor learns through the squashed draw. So the whole equation says this: the centre plus the width times a fresh random number, squashed into -1 to 1, is the actor's drawn torques.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Example. A large unsquashed draw lands near the torque limit after squashing, never past it, so the arm never plays a torque its joints cannot give.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: So the actor's drawn torques are the centre plus the width times a fresh random number, squashed into -1 to 1.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: Take the arm holding still with its hand off the goal. The actor's centre points the torques one way and its width spreads them, so each fresh draw lands somewhere near the centre and the squashed torques stay inside what the joints can give. When the centre moves toward the goal and the width stays open, the arm tries nearby torques instead of repeating one wild swing.

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: 3.4 The actor's loss

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The actor's loss

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together

units.section: 3 How reward, target, draw and temperature fit together
units.spoken: The mathematics. L of alpha is the temperature's loss. The E is the average over the actor's draws, weighted by their chance. alpha h is the temperature times this draw's surprise, minus the log of the draw's chance; alpha H bar is the temperature times the target entropy H bar . The slope is h minus the target entropy, and each step moves alpha against that slope: a negative slope, when the bell is too narrow, nudges alpha up, and a positive slope nudges it down. This replaces hand-tuning alpha : the loss sets the temperature while training runs. Torques are real-valued, they can take any value in their range, so the bell's height is a density, how much of the draw piles up near one torque, and not a chance that stops at one. A narrow bell is tall, so its height can pass one, and surprise is minus the log of that height: when the height passes one the log is positive, so the surprise is negative, and the average surprise, the entropy, can go below zero. So the whole equation says this: the temperature rises when draws are too likely and falls when they are too unlikely.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: Section five, SAC's actor and update in PyTorch

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: PyTorch is a code library for building and training networks. The code below uses its building blocks, and each one is explained in the notes under the code.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: This block imports the pieces the code needs: the torch library, the network building blocks, the bell the actor draws from, and the loss functions.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: The imports: torch is the library, nn builds networks, Normal is the bell the actor draws from, and F carries the loss functions. EPS_GUARD is 1e-6, the tiny guard constant that avoids the log of zero. HIDDEN is 256, the width of both hidden layers.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: This block defines the actor as a squashed bell: a network that returns a centre and a log width for each state.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: First, the network: it returns one centre and one log width per torque. The network outputs the log of the width, so the width stays positive. nn.Module means this class is a network, nn.Sequential stacks layers in a row, nn.Linear is one layer of weights, and ReLU passes positive signals and turns negative ones to zero.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: This block is the actor's draw: it takes a state, draws a fresh random number, builds the unsquashed draw, squashes it, and returns the draw with its log-probability.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: Next, the draw: a fresh random draw is scaled by the width, shifted by the centre and squashed into the torque range. torch.randn_like draws fresh random numbers shaped like the centre.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: Last, the log-probability of the squashed draw. Squashing piles torques up near -1 and 1, so the likelihood of a squashed torque is corrected by the second term. Normal(m, std).log_prob(u) is the log-probability of the draw.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: One helper blends the slow copies.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: This block is the slow-copy helper: it blends each slow weight a small share toward its live weight.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: The slow-copy helper: each slow weight moves a share tau toward its live weight, so the slow copies trail the live networks a little at a time.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: One update step runs in two parts.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: This block is the first half of one update: it builds the target and moves both live critics toward the shared target.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: First, the target: under torch.no_grad() the target is a fixed number, not trained. The target is the reward plus the discount times the lower slow score minus the temperature times the log-probability of the next draw. Both live critics move toward the one shared target. F.mse_loss is the mean squared gap between a critic's score and the target. critic_opt is the optimizer that takes the critics' step. critic_opt.zero_grad() clears the critics' gradients first, so one update's gradients do not pile into the next. Each .backward() call runs a backward pass, which works out how each weight should move to shrink its loss.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: Then the actor, the temperature, the copies.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: This block is the second half of one update: the actor loss, the temperature loss, and the slow copies blending.

units.section: 5 SAC's actor and update in PyTorch
units.spoken: Next, the actor loss and the temperature loss: the actor loss climbs the lower live critic while keeping the bell wide. The temperature loss uses log alpha in place of alpha, which keeps alpha positive, and detach means use this value but do not pass slopes through it. The leading minus sign and the plus inside turn logp, which is minus the surprise, into surprise minus the target entropy, so the code matches the temperature loss with log alpha standing in for alpha. After the temperature step, alpha is refreshed from log alpha, then each slow critic blends a small step toward its live critic. actor_opt takes the actor's step and alpha_opt takes the temperature's step. actor_opt.zero_grad() and alpha_opt.zero_grad() clear the actor's and the temperature's gradients before their backward passes.

sections.section: 6 How the temperature sets the bell's width

units.section: 6 How the temperature sets the bell's width
units.spoken: Section six, How the temperature sets the bell's width

units.section: 6 How the temperature sets the bell's width
units.spoken: The tool below shows one torque with two equally good ways to turn the shoulder. Raise the temperature and watch the bell widen until it covers both, or switch on automatic tuning and watch it find the width itself.

units.section: 6 How the temperature sets the bell's width
units.spoken: Try the tool. Set the temperature with the slider and watch the bell widen until it covers both regions. At the top of the slider the bell is so wide that the critic's two regions barely shape it. Or switch on automatic tuning and watch it step the temperature a little at a time until it stops, with the bell sitting in the target band.

units.section: 6 How the temperature sets the bell's width
units.spoken: Let's take a look at figure 6. A bell of torques stands over two equally good regions, with the critic's score under it and sampled draws from the bell. So the temperature sets how wide the bell stays: at low temperature it sits narrow over one region, and at high temperature it covers both.

units.section: 6 How the temperature sets the bell's width
units.spoken: At low temperature the bell sits narrow over one region; at high temperature it covers both regions, so some draws land in the dip between them. The gauge shows the bell's width against the target entropy band: the teal square is the target band and the orange dash is the bell's width now, and the dots are sampled draws from the bell. The automatic switch steps the temperature until the bell sits in the band, covering both ways to turn the shoulder.

sections.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: Section seven, How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: 7.1 One gradient step for every step the arm takes

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: After every step the arm takes, one gradient step, one move of the weights in the direction that shrinks a loss, runs for the critics, the actor and alpha, then the slow copies blend.

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: Memory is dominated by the replay buffer, one million stored steps; the networks add five sets of weights, the actor, two live critics and two slow critics.

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: Evaluation means testing the trained actor with exploration switched off. At evaluation the arm uses the centre of the bell, not a random draw.

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: Stable-Baselines3, a widely used reinforcement learning code library, runs this update.

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: 7.2 SAC's own setting: the target entropy

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: SAC adds one setting of its own: the target entropy is minus the number of torques. The temperature is not a fixed value: it is tuned automatically to hold the actor's surprise at the target entropy. A higher target entropy holds the bell wider and the temperature higher; a lower target entropy lets the bell narrow.

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: SAC once tuned a reward scale per task instead; a reward scale means multiplying every reward by a number, which changes how much reward weighs against the entropy bonus. Tuning the temperature automatically replaces it.

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: 7.3 SAC against PPO and against its deterministic variant

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: The comparison runs SAC and Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) on six simulated robot tasks in the SAC paper: Hopper, a one-legged hopper; Walker, a two-legged walker; HalfCheetah, a running cheetah body; Ant, a four-legged crawler; Humanoid, a human-shaped robot; and Humanoid in rllab, a taller human-shaped robot from the rllab suite, the hardest of the six. PPO is another way to train an actor: it makes small, careful updates and learns only from fresh steps, while SAC reuses each stored step many times from its replay memory. A seed is one full training run started from its own random start. Each method is scored by the return its trained actor earns, and each is run from several seeds.

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: On the harder three, Ant, Humanoid and Humanoid in rllab, SAC scored higher than PPO and the other baselines, and its scores barely moved from one seed to the next. On the easier three, Hopper, Walker and HalfCheetah, SAC scored about the same as PPO.

units.section: 7 How SAC is trained and how it compares with PPO and the deterministic variant
units.spoken: SAC is compared with a deterministic variant that does not reward staying undecided and closely resembles DDPG. A hard copy overwrites the slow copy with the live weights every so often. This variant keeps two critics, updates their slow copies by hard copies, has no slow actor and explores with fixed noise. The paper's appendix runs the deterministic variant on the same six tasks, where it performs comparably to SAC on all but Humanoid in rllab, on which SAC is the fastest. In a separate test on Humanoid in rllab alone, the deterministic variant's scores varied widely from one seed to the next, while SAC's stayed steady.

units.section: 8 When SAC fits
units.spoken: Section eight, When SAC fits

units.section: 8 When SAC fits
units.spoken: SAC fits continuous actions where steps are costly, as on real robots, where exploration matters, or where settings must work across tasks without tuning. Prefer Twin Delayed DDPG (TD3) for a deterministic actor and slightly simpler code; Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) when fresh steps are cheap.

units.section: 8 When SAC fits
units.spoken: The test is three questions: are the steps costly, as on a real robot, does the arm need to keep exploring, and must one set of settings work across tasks without tuning? The Minitaur passes all three, since falls cost time, the gait must keep exploring, and the same settings must work on flat ground and on stairs.

units.section: 9 How SAC fails
units.spoken: Section nine, How SAC fails

units.section: 9 How SAC fails
units.spoken: Fixed temperature too high. The bonus for staying undecided outweighs the reward, so the actor stays nearly random and ignores the goal. Automatic tuning, or a lower fixed temperature, lets the reward count again.

units.section: 9 How SAC fails
units.spoken: Fixed temperature too low. The bonus counts for almost nothing, so the bell narrows early and the arm locks onto the first gait that works, even a poor one. Raising the temperature keeps the bell open longer.

units.section: 9 How SAC fails
units.spoken: Missing tanh correction. Squashing piles torques up near the limits, so the bell's entropy is measured wrongly there and automatic tuning holds the bell at the wrong width. Adding the correction to the log-probability measures the squashed draw's likelihood right. No paper states this failure mode; it follows from the correction.

units.section: 9 How SAC fails
units.spoken: Evaluating with random draws. Random draws score lower than the bell's best torques, so the scores look worse than the trained actor really is. Evaluating with the centre of the bell shows what the actor has actually learned.

units.section: 9 How SAC fails
units.spoken: Soft-update share too large. The slow critics track the live critics too fast, so the target moves almost as fast as the scores chasing it and training goes unstable. A smaller share holds the target nearly still.

units.section: 9 How SAC fails
units.spoken: Reward scale changed with a fixed temperature. Scaling the rewards changes how much reward weighs against the entropy bonus, so the same fixed temperature acts too high or too low. Automatic tuning, or retuning the scale, restores the balance.

sections.section: 10 Practicing inside a model of the world

units.section: 10 Practicing inside a model of the world
units.spoken: Section ten, Practicing inside a model of the world

units.section: 10 Practicing inside a model of the world
units.spoken: SAC still learns only from steps the real arm takes, and every one of those steps costs time and wear. Model-based reinforcement learning is next in the series: it learns a model of the world so the arm can practice inside the model instead of on the real robot, and fewer real steps are needed, the Minitaur's concern, since falls cost time and can damage it.
